title: Kangju Sun
text:
Hi, I’m Kangju Sun. I am currently a Master of Data Science student at the University of British Columbia.
I studied Mathematics at UBC before starting the MDS program. I am interested in data analysis, statistics, and practical applications of data science.
This website will include some of my work and experiences during the MDS program.

title: Two Months of Pool Practice
text:
After finishing my undergraduate courses, I had about two months of free time. I started playing pool more regularly again.
I was curious whether spending more time practicing each week would be related to how I performed in my weekly games. I created a small dataset representing eight weeks of practice and competition results.

pool_data <- data.frame(
  week = 1:8,
  practice_hours = c(4, 6, 5, 8, 10, 7, 12, 11),
  matches_won = c(1, 2, 1, 3, 4, 3, 5, 4)
)

title: Two Months of Pool Practice
text:
Practice Time
First, I looked at my average weekly practice time.

mean(pool_data$practice_hours)

[1] 7.875


I also calculated the average number of matches won each week.

mean(pool_data$matches_won)

[1] 2.875

title: Two Months of Pool Practice
text:
Practice and Competition Results
To see whether practice time and competition results moved together, I calculated their correlation.

cor(pool_data$practice_hours, pool_data$matches_won)

[1] 0.9757264


A positive correlation would mean that weeks with more practice tended to also have better competition results.

title: Two Months of Pool Practice
text:
Visualizing the Relationship

plot(
  pool_data$practice_hours,
  pool_data$matches_won,
  xlab = "Practice Hours per Week",
  ylab = "Matches Won",
  main = "Pool Practice and Weekly Results",
  pch = 19
)

abline(
  lm(matches_won ~ practice_hours, data = pool_data)
)








The plot suggests a positive relationship between practice time and matches won. In this small example, the weeks when I practiced more generally also had better results.
Of course, practice time is not the only thing that affects a pool match. Opponents, concentration, and how I played on that particular day could also matter.

title: Hello World
text:
My first few weeks in the MDS program have been busy. There are many new courses, assignments, and tools, so I am still getting used to the pace.
One big change for me is using Git, GitHub, R, Python, and Quarto much more often. My undergraduate background is in Mathematics, so some of these tools are still new to me.
The first few weeks have been challenging, but I am slowly getting more comfortable with the program. I hope I can become faster with the technical tools and focus more on data science as the program continues.

title: About
text:
My name is Kangju Sun. I studied Mathematics at UBC and I am currently a Master of Data Science student.
I have experience with Python, R, Excel, and SQL. I am interested in data science, statistics, and data analysis.
I hope to use this website to record some of my work and experiences during the MDS program.
